scope: fixtures/rendering (whole project: src/Leaderboard.tsx, src/TodoList.tsx; package.json and tsconfig.json read as context)

findings.title: Full 50k-row sort and filter run on every keystroke
findings.explanation: `query` is component state, so each keystroke in the search input re-renders Leaderboard. Every render copies and sorts the entire `players` array and then filters it, although only 20 rows are shown. The size is evidenced by the comment on line 5 (about 50,000 rows loaded in one request) and the frequency by the `onChange` handler on line 14 (every keystroke). The sort depends only on `players`, not on `query`, so it is recomputed for no reason on each keystroke. Impact: each keystroke blocks the main thread for an O(n log n) sort over about 50k items before the input can paint. The cost was not measured. If the real list is much smaller, the severity drops to low.
findings.evidence:
const ranked = [...players].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
  const visible = ranked.filter((p) => p.name.includes(query)).slice(0, 20);
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the sorted array once per `players` change, for example `const ranked = useMemo(() => [...players].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score), [players]);`, then filter and slice on each render. Optionally wrap `query` in `useDeferredValue` if filtering is still slow. Verify the gain by profiling typing in the component.

findings.title: Array index used as key on a reorderable list whose rows hold uncontrolled input state
findings.explanation: The list is keyed by index (`key={i}`), but each row holds state in its DOM input (`defaultValue={t.text}`), and the parent removes items by id through `onRemove(t.id)`. When an item before the end is removed, the remaining rows shift up. React reuses the row instance at each index, and `defaultValue` is applied only on mount, so the input at index 0 keeps the text that was typed into the removed row and now sits next to the next todo. The visible text and any edits end up attached to the wrong todo. Concrete failure: type into row 1, remove row 0, and row 0 now shows row 1's typed text. Impact: the wrong text is shown and edited after any non-last removal. The fix is safe because each todo has a stable `id`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the stable id as the key: `{todos.map((t, i) => (<li key={t.id}>...))}`. If the input should follow the todo text, make it controlled (`value` plus `onChange` from the parent) instead of relying on `defaultValue`. The `aria-label` can keep using `i + 1` for display.

limitations: Runtime behaviour was not executed. The F1 cost estimate and the 50k-row size are taken from the comment on src/Leaderboard.tsx line 5 and are not measured. If the real size is small, F1 drops to low.
